subject: Urgent: Quicksave reserved throughput mismatch — bridging plan & exec ask
messages:
From: Erin Walsh <erin@quicksave.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Quicksave Procurement <procurement@quicksave.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -0000
Subject: Production latency/5xx spike + reserved throughput not matching committed profile

Vanessa —

We're seeing a sharp rise in tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors across our inference calls starting ~06:30 PT. Our monitoring shows sessions hitting token backpressure and apparent queueing despite our reserved capacity setting. This is causing timeouts in the payment auth flow and two retries already triggered order failures.

I attached a short sample of 5xx traces (qs_prod_5xx_sample.log) and a snapshot of the client-side observed latency. Important context: our contract (QS-2026-EXP-47) committed to 1.2k qps steady-state with 100ms p95 SLO. We're currently seeing p95 ~420ms and sustained 500-range errors for ~18 minutes.

Please advise immediate mitigation and whether this counts toward an SLA credit event. We need an exec-level bridge if this can't be resolved in 30 minutes.

—Erin
Erin Walsh
Head of Engineering, Quicksave
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Walsh <erin@quicksave.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production latency/5xx spike + reserved throughput not matching committed profile

Erin — thanks for the flag and attachments. We're pulling an on-call runbook now. Naomi (CS) and I are standing up an ops bridge. Can you confirm the exact time window and whether any traffic pattern changes occurred client-side (batching, prompt length spike)?

Immediate asks from our side:
- Share a short trace with request ids (if available) so we can correlate to infra logs.
- If possible, drop a prod sample with the smaller payload that hit the 5xx so we can exclude prompt-related OOM.

Naomi — I'm assigning you ownership for the customer bridge. David, FYI — procurement looped in; we may need an interim credit/burst authorization depending on root cause.

I'll update within 10 minutes with next steps.

—Vanessa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Walsh <erin@quicksave.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 08:28:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production latency/5xx spike + reserved throughput not matching committed profile

Erin — I'm on the bridge. We see correlated errors in our serving telemetry: token queue depth climbed and KV cache hit rate dropped for Quicksave's model shard. Marcus — can you confirm whether a background quantization job or scheduled rebalancer ran in the US-WEST region around 06:20–06:40 PT?

I've attached kv-cache-stats-20261209.csv (brief) and a pointer to the incident trace.

Erin, I'm keeping the bridge pinned; please post any request ids. We'll triage root cause (noisy neighbor vs. reserved-capacity regression) and propose a short remediation path (burst routing, temporary model downgrade, or immediate slot bump).

—Naomi
Senior Customer Success Manager
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Erin Walsh <erin@quicksave.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production latency/5xx spike + reserved throughput not matching committed profile

Quick technical summary:
- No scheduled rebalancer/quantization occurred in that window.
- We observed a reservoir of long-running KV cache fills from a new cosine-similarity batch job tied to a Quicksave internal feature (Erin, any recent client deploys that could cause longer context windows?)
- Auto-batcher thresholds misfired under a high-tail distribution; a recent bundling optimization increased request-grouping aggressiveness. That optimization rolled to the US pool last week.

Immediate mitigations we can implement (ETA shown):
1) Roll back the bundling optimization for Quicksave's route (ETA 18m) — reduces per-request queueing.
2) Route a fraction of traffic to a spare dedicated pool (requires temporary burst capacity authorization; ETA 10m to flip routing once capacity authorized).
3) Apply a soft prompt-length cap at edge (client-ack required; ETA 6m) — fastest, but degrades some requests.

Dylan will stand up a short-run patch for 1) and test. If routing changes are required, we need ops approval for reserved slot reallocation.

—Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Walsh <erin@quicksave.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production latency/5xx spike + reserved throughput not matching committed profile — decision and next steps

Erin — thank you for your patience. Quick readout from the bridge and leadership alignment:

Findings (summary):
- Root cause: a combination of Quicksave's new background batching workload causing longer-lived KV cache population and an aggressive bundling change in our auto-batcher that increased queue depth for bursty traffic patterns. Not a quota assignment failure; reserved capacity was available but transient headroom was consumed by long-lived KV tasks.

Actions taken:
- Rolled back the bundling optimization on Quicksave's route (completed 10:30 PT).
- Temporarily routed 20% of production traffic to a warm spare dedicated pool (10:45 PT); this required a one-off burst approval from ops and cost cover from an internal contingency.
- Applied a short-term edge prompt-length guard for 15 minutes to drain queues (11:00 PT).

Current status: error-rate reduced to baseline, p95 improved from 420ms -> 110ms within ~45 minutes. No further 5xx spikes observed. Attached is the mutual_action_plan_QS_v1.pdf with proposed long-term changes and checkpoints.

Executive ask: David and I are requesting a formal one-time burst credit to Quicksave for the incident window (deal QS-2026-EXP-47). Proposed credit: capped 10% of last-month usage or a fixed $12.5k (whichever is lower) — we recommend this as a customer-experience gesture while engineering implements a durable fix (batching tuning + explicit KV cache isolation).

Next steps and owners:
- Marcus: durable auto-batcher tuning and a feature flag to exempt reserved routes (ETA 3 days).
- Dylan: add telemetry to catch long-lived KV fills and trigger autoscaling earlier (ETA 48h).
- Naomi: schedule a joint post-incident review with Quicksave and share the MAP (ETA 48h).
- David: lead procurement/credit conversation with Quicksave and confirm the acceptance path (ETA 24h).

Erin — can you confirm whether the proposed credit approach is acceptable, or if procurement needs an alternative structure? We'll keep the bridge open for any follow-up.

—Vanessa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
